approach: Root cause: a job cut on an earlier unmerged job's branch has its dependency written nowhere, and nothing after a merge looks at the earlier pull requests that merge carries. Fix in two parts. (1) PrLink (pr.rs) gains a defaulted `base_jobs` field. `land_pr` fills it for an open link with the other jobs whose open link head is an ancestor of the job's landing commit; a new `pr::all_links` reads both link locations. (2) After `land_pr` sees its own link Landed, a new `close_carried_prs` (landing.rs) walks `base_jobs`, and through each earlier link's own `base_jobs` the rest of the stack. For each earlier PR it asks the host for state and current head, skips any PR that is not open, and closes it (with a comment naming the merging PR and merged commit) only when that head is an ancestor of the merged commit or of the exact head the host merged (the second arm covers squash merges, which leave no ancestry). Closing uses two new PrHost methods, `pr_status` and `close_pr`, with default error bodies. Every failure becomes a PrReport.warnings entry; the merge, landing record and stored link are never undone. Scope note answering the round-1 findings: the only edits outside the listed deliverables are (a) one mechanical line `base_jobs: Vec::new()` at each existing PrLink struct literal in early.rs, after_merge_tests.rs, display.rs, drain.rs and external_calls.rs, because Rust requires every field in a literal and criteria 2 and 8 need the field and a compiling workspace; no behavior changes there; and (b) docs/design/native-pr-landing.md, the only doc that mentions pr-link and lists its fields (lines 151-153), which criterion 7 requires updated. No other out-of-list file is touched; main.rs is deliberately left unchanged.

decisions.choice: Record `base_jobs: Vec<String>` on PrLink with #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Vec::is_empty")], filled inside `land_pr` for an open link by testing which other open links' heads are ancestors of `job.commit`.
decisions.reason: `land_pr` runs for both a link it just published and one adopted from the early step, so one site covers both. It already holds Ancestry and StateDir, so `LandPr` gets no new field and its construction sites stay untouched. Ancestry is exactly 'built on that job's branch' with no trailer parsing, which works before and after C0. Skip-if-empty keeps unstacked links byte-identical on disk.

rejected.option: Compute the base job from git history in Athena::land_pr and pass it in a new LandPr field
rejected.why: After C0 commits carry no trailers; a new LandPr field breaks every `LandPr {` literal; detecting bases from history for landed jobs is out of scope.

rejected.option: Record the earlier PR number instead of the job id
rejected.why: The number is not known when the later job is cut; the job id keys into the state-directory link that holds number and head.

rejected.option: Record nothing and scan all open links after a merge
rejected.why: That is the 'no recorded dependency' behavior named as the root cause, and criterion 2 requires the field.

decisions.choice: Carried test: the earlier PR's head as the host reports it now is an ancestor of the merged commit, OR an ancestor of the merging link's head (the commit the host was told to merge). An ancestry Err counts as 'not carried' for that arm; if neither arm holds and one errored, leave the PR open and warn.
decisions.reason: The brief's rule is 'every commit reachable from the merged commit'. The repository squash-merges (docs/design/native-pr-landing.md, D88), so a squash commit has main as its only parent and the earlier head is never its ancestor; the first arm alone would never fire in production. The merge is guarded by the head sha, so a head that is an ancestor of it has all its content in main. Using the host's current head means a later push to the earlier branch is judged too, and an unreachable new commit keeps the PR open.

rejected.why: Never closes anything after a squash merge, so stale PRs would stay.
Out of scope ('any rule other than all commits reachable') and could close a PR whose content a later job changed.

decisions.choice: Run the reconciliation at the end of `land_pr` whenever the link is Landed, including a run that finds the PR already merged. It never returns an error.
decisions.reason: Covers a merge made by the host's setting or by hand, and retries a close that failed earlier. Closed PRs read as not open, so repeats are idempotent.

rejected.option: Run only on the call that sends the merge request
rejected.why: A manual merge or a failed close would never be reconciled.
It takes only &dyn Host and has no ancestry or close capability; widening it changes its callers.

decisions.choice: Add PrHost::pr_status(number) -> PrStatus { state: PrState (Open, Merged, Closed), head } and PrHost::close_pr(number, comment), both with default bodies returning an error. GhClient overrides: GET pulls/N; PATCH pulls/N state=closed, then POST issues/N/comments. All three log HostOperation::ReadPr.
decisions.reason: Defaults keep the other PrHost implementors (test_support.rs FakeHost and EarlyFake, tests.rs RunHost) compiling with no edit, so no extra files change. HostOperation is a closed list in athena-data that the watcher parses; client.rs rerun_failed already reuses an existing variant for the same reason. Closing first then commenting means a failed comment leaves the PR closed and the warning says so.

rejected.why: Forces edits to every fake in out-of-list files for no behavioral gain.

decisions.choice: Do not add LinkState::Closed or a carried_by field on the earlier link; the host's PR state is the authority.
decisions.reason: A new variant reaches every exhaustive match on LinkState (display.rs and others), and writing another job's link file would bypass that job's lock.

risks.risk: Some stale PRs stay open: after rebase_job_branch replays an earlier job's commit under a new hash its published head is no longer an ancestor of the later head; or an earlier job's link was already cleaned so it was never recorded.
risks.mitigation: The failure is on the safe side: the PR is left open, and a warning names it when the ancestry check errors. Detecting such PRs from history is out of scope. The CHANGELOG states the rule.

risks.risk: The earlier job's PR is closed while its stored link still says Open, so a later `athena land <earlier job>` would try to merge a closed PR.
risks.mitigation: No worse than the old state (it would merge an empty change). The host refuses a merge on a closed PR and land reports it. No new link state is added, to avoid touching every LinkState match.

risks.risk: A close succeeds and the comment then fails, leaving a closed PR with no explanation.
risks.mitigation: The comment is posted after the close; its failure becomes a warning naming the PR and saying it is closed. The warning text is asserted in a test.

risks.risk: Wrongly closing live work, e.g. an earlier PR with a newer commit not in the merge.
risks.mitigation: The host's current head is judged, not the recorded one; closing needs the PR Open and its head an ancestor. The head-e2 test and the Merged/Closed test guard it.

risks.risk: A concurrent process writes another job's pr-link.json while it is read ([parallel] max_concurrency path).
risks.mitigation: The step only reads other links; a read or parse error is a warning that skips that link; it never writes another job's file. The merging job's own lock covers its own link.

risks.risk: Editing docs trips the ontology or budget tests.
risks.mitigation: Add sentences only; leave marker lines (docs/ontology.toml:56,128,129) unchanged; run `cargo test --locked` before finishing.

risks.risk: A PrLink literal is missed, breaking compilation in a crate outside the listed deliverables.
risks.mitigation: The nine literal sites found by grep of `PrLink {` are all listed; the producer searches `PrLink {` again and runs the full `cargo test --locked`, which fails to compile on any miss.
